title: WPSS/668/2013 of Vinod Goswami Vs Secretary Uttarakhand Board Of Technical Education AND ANOTHER

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/S) No. 668 of 2013
Vinod Goswami Ö Petitioner
Vs
Secretary, Uttarakhand Board of Technical
Education & another Ö Respondents
Mr. K.N. Joshi, Advocate, present for the petitioner
Mr. Subhash Upadhyay, Standing Counsel, present for the State of Uttarakhand
Mr. Rakesh Thapliyal, Advocate, present for respondent
Honíble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J. (Oral)
1. The petitioner was an Other Backward Class (in
short ëO.B.C.í) category candidate, which is a reserved
category, as well as dependant of Freedom Fighter applied for
the post of ìCane Supervisorî. Since for the post of Cane
Supervisor there was no reservation for O.B.C. candidate,
therefore, the petitioner was considered only in the said
selection as a General category candidate.
2. The petitioner further claims reservation as
dependent of Freedom Fighter. The petitioner has got 26.25
marks in the written examination.
3. Since the petitioner was being considered as a
General candidate, he claims horizontal reservation as a
dependent of a Freedom Fighter in the General category
candidate. This has, however, been denied by the
respondents. According to the respondents, the petitioner
cannot get horizontal reservation in the O.B.C. category
candidate as there is no reservation for O.B.C. The petitioner
is an O.B.C. candidate, he would be given reservation of
O.B.C. only in those posts which are reserved for O.B.C.
Since for all practical purposes the petitioner is competing as
a General category candidate, therefore, he is also liable to be
given all the benefits which are given to the General category
candidate which should include horizontal reservation to

2
dependents of Freedom Fighter.
4. This controversy has also been disposed of by this
Court in a writ petition (WPSS No. 435 of 2013) wherein it has
been held that since the petitioner was competing, though
belong to O.B.C. candidate, as a General category candidate
as there was no post reserved for O.B.C. candidate, he was
also liable to given all benefits which are given to General
category candidate in Horizontal reservation of dependent of
Freedom Fighter.
5. In view of the above, the writ petition is disposed
of with the direction that the candidate who has obtained
highest marks in the General category and dependent
Freedom Fighter be given appointment, treating the petitioner
to be a General category candidate for the purpose of granting
benefit as a dependent of Freedom Fighter candidate.
6. It is made clear that a clarification was already
made in the order dated 04.09.2013 passed in WPSS No. 435
of 2013 that if any candidate of the same category has more
marks then the petitioner, his claim has to be considered first.
The respondents should take a decision keeping in mind the
decision dated 04.09.2013 given in WPSS No. 435 of 2013 as
well as directions given in the present writ petition.
7. No order as to costs.
(Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
06.09.2013
Aswal
